scenario: Tomas applied for naturalization. During the statutory period he was convicted once for a drug offense involving marijuana. He has no other criminal history and meets all residence requirements.
policy: An applicant for naturalization must demonstrate good moral character during the statutory period. A conviction for an aggravated felony at any time permanently bars a finding of good moral character; a single conviction for simple possession of 30g or less of marijuana does NOT bar good moral character.
question: Is Tomas barred from establishing good moral character based on this conviction?
